spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap is the dominant cost driver; we set a default that's long enough to reveal spirals but capped
spec_features.evidence: config.py:108 max_turns:int=30; runner.py:166 `for turn in range(1, cfg.max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop and breaks at the budget (Transcript.stop_reason default 'max_turns' at runner.py:52). The cap is read and enforced as the loop bound.
spec_features.notes: Hard upper bound on number of turns the subject is driven; enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns | 30 | enough for spiral to develop; capped for cost  (config field comment / defaults); config.py module docstring: 'cost/reproduction-rate trade-offs ... explicit knobs'

spec_features.feature_name: spiral onset measurement to recommend minimum turn budget
spec_features.spec_quote: We measure when the spiral onset happens so we can recommend the *minimum* turn budget that still reproduces
spec_features.evidence: onset is computed (_detect_onset metrics.py:246, set on m.onset_turn at metrics.py:168) and aggregated to a median for reporting only (analyze.py:67-68,107-108 det_onset_turn_median; report line analyze.py:222). No code path uses onset to reduce max_turns, recommend a minimal budget, or otherwise act on it — it is purely measured and printed.
spec_features.notes: Value is recorded/reported but never acted on, so by the strict scale this is 'no' (measured but not enforced as a minimization).

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop heuristic (optional): if deterministic metrics already cross the spiral threshold with high confidence, we can stop early
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:235-240: `if cfg.early_stop_on_det and turn >= cfg.onset_window + 2: m = deterministic_metrics(...); if spiral_index(m, cfg.weights) >= cfg.early_stop_det_threshold: tr.stop_reason = 'early_stop_det'; break`. Mechanism is fully wired — computes D_det, compares to threshold, and breaks the loop. Default off (config.py:early_stop_on_det=False) but enforced when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced exit when toggled on; off by default. Rated yes because the mechanism runs and changes execution when the flag is set.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Optional cost saver: stop a run early once D_det is confidently high. Off by default to keep transcripts comparable (config.py comment)

spec_features.feature_name: termination on turn budget or well-formed stop signal
spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends only on the turn budget or an explicit, well-formed stop signal from the model
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:213-227: if model emits no tool calls, no_action_streak increments; at stop_patience(=2) it sets stop_reason='no_action_stop' and breaks (after one nudge). Also giveup break at 207-210 and max_turns bound at 166. submit explicitly does NOT end the loop (tools.py tool_submit). So the loop ends on budget or a model stop signal, as claimed.
spec_features.notes: Stop pathway is honored end-to-end. submit is intentionally not a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nudge once, then accept the stop as graceful/abandonment.

spec_features.feature_name: system-prompt 'you may stop if a task is impossible' (permit_stopping)
spec_features.spec_quote: system-prompt "you may stop if a task is impossible" on/off
spec_features.evidence: config.py PressureProfile.permit_stopping(bool); prompts.py:30-33 build_system_prompt appends _PERMIT_STOP ('...you may stop and clearly report that conclusion instead of continuing') when permit_stopping is True. The text is actually delivered to the subject, and the referenced stop is honored by the no_action_stop pathway (runner.py:215-220). Default high preset has permit_stopping=False, but 'low'/'medium' presets enable it (config.py:43-49).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered AND a stop pathway exists to honor it. On/off via preset.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Tell the model in the system prompt that it MAY stop if a task is impossible. permit_stopping: bool = False

spec_features.spec_quote: give-up tool exposed on/off (does an explicit exit hatch reduce spirals?)
spec_features.evidence: config.py PressureProfile.expose_giveup_tool; runner.py:96-99 _exposed_tool_names appends 'giveup' when set; prompts.py:34-36 advertises the tool; tools.py tool_giveup returns meta={'giveup':True}; runner.py:200-202 sets gave_up; runner.py:207-210 `if gave_up: tr.gave_up=True; tr.stop_reason='giveup'; break`. Fully wired: exposed -> dispatched -> honored as a loop-ending stop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end exit hatch; enabled only in 'low' preset (config.py:43-46).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Explicit graceful-exit affordance, only present under low-pressure ablations. (tool_giveup docstring)
